Code & results
Conformance · KubeMQ against Apache Kafka 4.3.1 · run 2026-10-17

Same client code. Same tests. Does KubeMQ behave like Kafka?

313 tests cover the Kafka protocol, client libraries, transactions, Kafka's own tools, security, operations and migration. Every test runs on real Apache Kafka first, then on KubeMQ with only the bootstrap address changed. A test passes when both brokers behave the same.

Run and published by KubeMQ. Read it with that in mind, and rerun it yourself: the suite, its method and every result are in the repository. The KubeMQ half needs an evaluation key from KubeMQ.

Optional features

Kafka features KubeMQ does not offer today. Each was listed before the run, with the exact behaviour the run had to observe; if the behaviour had changed, the test would have failed.

FeatureWho is affectedWorkaround
Kafka Streams new rebalance protocol (KIP-1071): heartbeat
apikey.88		Kafka Streams with group.protocol=streams (KIP-1071) cannot join a group.Run Streams applications with the classic rebalance protocol, the Kafka Streams default.
Kafka Streams new rebalance protocol (KIP-1071): describe
apikey.89		kafka-streams-groups.sh and Admin describe for KIP-1071 streams groups; such groups cannot exist on KubeMQ.Describe classic Streams groups with kafka-consumer-groups.sh.
eligible.leader.replicas.version feature flag
feature.eligible.leader.replicas.version		kafka-features.sh describe and other tools that read this flag do not see it on KubeMQ. No client behaviour depends on it: the flags clients negotiate (transaction.version, group.version, metadata.version) are advertised as on Kafka.None needed for clients.
streams.version feature flag
feature.streams.version		kafka-features.sh describe and other tools that read this flag do not see it on KubeMQ. No client behaviour depends on it: the flags clients negotiate (transaction.version, group.version, metadata.version) are advertised as on Kafka.None needed for clients.
Broker-side topic compression
features.produce.broker-recompression		A topic created with compression.type=gzip (or any codec other than producer) keeps the batches in the producer's codec on KubeMQ; Kafka recompresses them. Consumers still decode every codec, so data is identical; only storage size and the codec consumers see differ. KubeMQ stores the per-topic comp ...Compress in the producer with the codec you want stored (compression.type on the producer).
OAUTHBEARER on the SASL_PLAINTEXT port
security.oauthbearer.plain-port		Clients that use OAUTHBEARER over SASL_PLAINTEXT (allowed by Kafka) cannot log in to KubeMQ; KubeMQ offers OAUTHBEARER on its SASL_SSL port by default.Connect OAUTHBEARER clients to the TLS port (SASL_SSL), or set CONNECTORS_KAFKA_OAUTH_BEARER_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT=true to offer it on the plaintext SASL port too.
Delegation tokens
security.delegation-tokens.create-and-login		kafka-delegation-tokens.sh and AdminClient createDelegationToken fail with DELEGATION_TOKEN_AUTH_DISABLED (61), the same answer a Kafka broker without a token secret gives; frameworks that hand delegation tokens to workers (Spark, Flink on secured Kafka) cannot use them.Give workers their own SCRAM credentials or mTLS certificates.
Kerberos (SASL/GSSAPI)
security.gssapi.configurable		Kerberos-authenticated fleets cannot connect; KubeMQ refuses GSSAPI in its mechanism list and does not start.Migrate those principals to SCRAM or mTLS.
Fixed 64 MiB log segment size
operations.config.segment-bytes		KubeMQ reports its real engine segment size (64 MiB); tools reading segment.bytes see that value; setting it has no effect (the engine segments by STORE_NEXT_SEGMENT_SIZE)None needed for clients.

What is tested

AreaWhat runs on both brokersTests
Kafka protocolEvery Kafka request type (ApiKey) and feature flag, compared with what Kafka advertises, plus full produce, fetch and transaction conversations replayed on both brokers and diffed.82
Broker behaviourProduce and fetch, acks, idempotence, consumer groups and rebalances, offsets, retention, compaction, topic administration and limits.59
Transactions and exactly-onceCommit, abort, read_committed, fencing, timeouts and exactly-once pipelines with the Java client, franz-go and librdkafka.23
Client librariesEach client's own quickstart with stock defaults, then produce, consume, consumer groups and commit and resume.25
ApplicationJava and Python order-processing services: compression, rebalancing groups and exactly-once pipelines with aborts, checked for no loss, no duplicates and per-customer order.1
Kafka tools and platformKafka's own CLI tools, Kafka Connect, Kafka Streams, MirrorMaker 2, lag monitors (Burrow, kafka-lag-exporter) and Kafbat UI, unmodified.44
SecurityTLS, mTLS, SASL PLAIN, SCRAM and OAUTHBEARER, re-authentication, ACLs and quotas, each configured the way the product documents it.41
Performance baselineKafka's own perf tools on both brokers on one machine. Measured, not judged.9
OperationsThe metrics, configuration answers and consumer lag an operator relies on, compared with Kafka's own.31
MigrationMoving topics and consumer-group offsets from Kafka to KubeMQ with MirrorMaker 2, cutting consumers over, and rolling back.7

Method

Real Apache Kafka is the reference. Every test runs against Kafka first, then against KubeMQ with only the bootstrap address changed; nothing else in the client, tool or scenario changes between the two. If the Kafka leg itself does not show the documented behaviour, the test proves nothing and is reported VOID, never PASS.

  • A difference is OPTIONAL only if it was listed, with the exact behaviour, before the run. Any other difference is a FAIL, and a FAIL is never relabelled afterwards.
  • A test that did not run fails the report; a skipped test is never quiet.
  • Every verifier ships a mutation test proving it reports FAIL on a lost, duplicated, reordered or misnumbered record.
  • Each test records its origin: an upstream Apache Kafka or client-project test, or one written by KubeMQ.

Full method: docs/methodology.md. Every difference in full: docs/gaps.md.

Run it yourself

You need Docker or podman, Go, curl, jq, lsof, git and a KubeMQ evaluation key. arm64 and amd64 both work. The suite pulls the latest KubeMQ image and the pinned Apache Kafka image, starts both on your machine and writes this same report.

git clone https://github.com/kubemq-io/kubemq-kafka-conformance.git
cd kubemq-kafka-conformance
export KUBEMQ_LICENSE_KEY=<your evaluation key>
runner/certify.sh --preflight-only   # checks your machine, starts nothing
runner/certify.sh --quick            # protocol tests, about 15 minutes
runner/certify.sh --full             # every test, 1 to 2 hours

Details: docs/rerun.md.

Run it against your own setup

The whole suite is in the repository. Point it at KubeMQ and Apache Kafka on your machine and get this same report, test by test.
